clue.text: Production of unusually neat region

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from the normal order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy part of the country turns out goods in an unexpected way.
explanation.definitionFit: Generation can mean the act of producing something, as in electricity generation, so it matches production.

clue.text: Grand period of time for fruit

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A splendid stretch of time spent waiting for fruit to ripen.
explanation.walkthrough: A gage is a plum, best known from greengage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gage is a variety of plum, so it is a kind of fruit; the greengage is the familiar example.

clue.text: Poverty-stricken houses having no free space, of necessity

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: needy people are poor
something full has no room left

explanation.surface: Poor families living in crammed housing because they have to.
explanation.walkthrough: Houses reads like a noun for homes, but it is the verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Needfully is an adverb meaning necessarily, matching the adverbial phrase of necessity.

clue.text: Civil or livid? Capital in either case using these?

definitions.text: Civil or livid? Capital in either case using these?

parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether someone is polite or furious

parts.words: Capital in either case using these?
parts.note: setter's reading: written in capitals, each of those two words is spelt entirely from letters standing for numbers in the ancient Italian system

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to stay polite or lose their temper, as if spelling it in capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: CIVIL is C, I, V, I, L and LIVID is L, I, V, I, D: every letter is a number to the Romans, written in upper case.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Romans wrote numbers with capital letters such as C, I, V, L and D, which spell both words.

clue.text: Descriptor of adolescents — between a dozen and a score!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adjective used of young people in their teens

definitions.text: between a dozen and a score
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an age lying after twelve and before twenty

explanation.walkthrough: A dozen is twelve and a score is twenty; the years between them are thirteen to nineteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes young people aged thirteen to nineteen, exactly the years between twelve and twenty.

clue.text: Evidently old forest greenery lay empty

parts.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old
vert is the old forest-law term for green vegetation in a forest

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, so only its first and last letters survive

parts.note: the outside letters of this word

explanation.surface: Old woodland foliage was plainly left lying bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert, from French for green, was the legal term for trees and undergrowth in a royal forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly or plainly, so something done overtly is evidently done.

clue.text: Little picture encapsulates impressive story

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the letters are found inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A small illustration that sums up a grand tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, grand narrative of heroic deeds, so it is an impressive story.

clue.text: Greek character with a large liquid container

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Greek person carrying a big container of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle used for holding medicines or other fluids.

clue.text: Film fan, one taken in by e.g. romance novel

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so this single letter goes within the rest
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take on a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged around the inserted one
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A movie lover gets absorbed in a romantic book.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters make CNEMAGOER, and I slips in after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinemagoer regularly watches films at the pictures, which makes them a film fan.

clue.text: Brightness of good well-organised male

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: organising something puts it into a new arrangement, so the following letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The cheerfulness of a decent, tidy man shines out.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a flash or glint of light, so it denotes brightness.

clue.text: Height of lean-to I've constructed

indicators.note: something constructed is built from parts, so these letters are assembled into a new word

parts.note: all nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reports how tall the shed they built is.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means altitude above a reference level, as in the elevation of a hill, so it is a height.

clue.text: The role that will or might could play?

definitions.text: The role that will or might could play?

parts.words: The role that will or might could play?
parts.note: surface reading: musing about what part willpower or strength could take
setter's reading: will, might and could are all helping verbs used with another verb in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what part determination or force might take in events.
explanation.walkthrough: Will and might look like nouns for resolve and power; read as grammar, they and could are helper verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, will, might and could are helping verbs that combine with a main verb to show mood or tense.

clue.text: Old-time visionary, enthusiast with discernment mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a fan is a keen supporter
good taste is discernment

explanation.surface: A dreamer of the past was keen and largely discerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantast is an archaic word for a dreamer or fanciful person, hence an old-time visionary.

clue.text: Plant tissue in waxy lemon

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A botanist points to tissue found in the peel of a shiny lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylem is the woody tissue that carries water up through vascular plants from the roots.

clue.text: Weapon succeeded with potentially urgent act

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: potentially means it could become something else, so these letters may be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon proved effective in a moment of emergency action.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattergun is a shotgun, a firearm spraying pellets widely, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Refinement in manners of sect by northern river

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Members of a religious group living by a river in the north show polished manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through North Yorkshire in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture can mean cultivated taste and polish in behaviour and the arts, a refinement of manners.

clue.text: We're told you will record this incandescent Christmas celebration

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound matters rather than spelling

parts.note: you will contracts to you'll, and to log is to record

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to note down a glowing festive tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: The yule log is a large log burned in the hearth at Christmas, also a chocolate cake shaped like one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log is burned in the fireplace over the festive season, so it glows as part of Christmas celebrations.

clue.text: According to Will, violently abuse country lady embracing knight

parts.note: a land is a country

indicators.note: embracing means holding within one's arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A noblewoman holding a knight in her arms, as Shakespeare might write it.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is Shakespeare, who uses this rare verb once, in The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's land-damn is usually glossed as to abuse or curse someone violently, perhaps to beat them.

clue.text: Your old inner being, the one the physician should heal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the archaic way of saying your own self

definitions.text: the one the physician should heal
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the proverb from Luke tells the doctor whom to cure first

explanation.walkthrough: The saying Physician, heal thyself comes from the Gospel of Luke.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyself is the archaic reflexive form of yourself, and the biblical proverb urges a physician to heal it.

clue.text: Vain and showy swimmer accepting work pressure

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
OP is short for opus, a work
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A conceited, flashy athlete in the pool takes on stress at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the crossword's usual shorthand for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Foppish describes a dandy overly concerned with clothes and looks, hence vain and showy.

clue.text: Shower interrupting support for probationer?

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle, so it is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A downpour stops play for a newcomer still on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The support is the golfer's peg that holds the ball before a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a job, often on a trial basis like a probationer.

clue.text: Essentially amateur, less powerful fine-tuner

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only the central letter is taken

parts.note: the central letter of this seven-letter word
weaker means having less power

explanation.surface: A hobbyist with less strength adjusts things only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweaker makes small adjustments to get something exactly right, which is what fine-tuning means.

clue.text: Additional craft recalled by one-time mate

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A former partner remembers some extra boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than is usual or expected, so it is a synonym of additional.

clue.text: Vagrant Frenchman caught by snare

indicators.note: something caught by a thing is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a snare is a trap
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur

explanation.surface: A wandering Frenchman is caught in a hunter's snare.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless person who wanders from place to place, a vagrant.

clue.text: Stewed pastry dish observed

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A slow-cooked pie is watched in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Stewed is slang for drunk, not a cooking term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for drunk, so stewed and pie-eyed mean the same thing.

clue.text: Boss stallion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ... on a surface
second meaning: a male horse kept for breeding

explanation.walkthrough: Boss looks like a manager, but here it is a raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a projecting knob like a stud, and a stud is also a stallion kept for breeding.

clue.text: Abnormal rage — out of sorts about ultimately defunct car device

indicators.note: abnormal means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: feeling sick means feeling out of sorts

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Unusual fury about a broken-down vehicle leaves the driver feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SICK after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A gearstick is the lever a driver moves to change gear, a control device in a car.

clue.text: Contents of memo satisfied worker, it's locally said

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the two inside letters of this word
to meet a demand is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: A note that kept an employee happy, as people round here put it.
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is a crossword term for an ant; emmet is a dialect word for one, used in Cornwall also for tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is a regional English word for an ant, and worker ants make the colony's labour force.

clue.text: Scruff's downy covering on middle of chest

parts.note: nap is the soft raised surface of cloth

indicators.note: middle points to the central letter of the next word only

parts.note: the central letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A scruffy person has fluff on their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Scruff looks like an untidy person, but it means the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, as in grabbing by the scruff, and the nape is that same area.

clue.text: Scanty money for rich, crumbly biscuit

parts.note: short means in short supply
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Little cash available for buying a luxurious biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich looks like it describes the person with money, but it belongs to the biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a buttery Scottish biscuit with a crumbly texture, rich from its high butter content.
